def: Any verb besides a ru-verb? or an irregular verb?. Also known as a Yodan or Group 1 verb. For example: 行く, 書く, and 読む.
Abbreviation for verb.
Abbreviation for noun.
Words or morphemes? that attach to the beginning of a word to change its meaning or grammatical (e.g., "大" in 大好き).
Words or morphemes? that attach to the end of a word to change its meaning or grammatical function (e.g., "さん" in 田中さん).
Verbs that ends with る but are not u-verbs (such as 走る and 帰る) or irregular verbs. Also known as Ichidan or Group 2 verbs. For example: 食べる, 寝る, and 着る.
Suru-verbs (e.g., する, 勉強する) and 来る.
The affirmative short non-past form for a verb.
Also known as the "nai" form in standard Japanese.
A collective term for the dictionary, simple past tense, and negative form. Also known as the plain form. For example 行く, 行かない, 行った, and 行かなかった.
Also known as the polite form or masu-form. For example: 行きます, 行きません, 行きました, and 行きませんでした.
The long (masu) verb form without the final "masu". This is also known as the pre-masu form. For example: 食べ, 行き, し, and き.
The short negative form? without the final "nai" in standard Japanese or "ん" in Kansai-ben. For example: 食べ, 行か, し, and こ in standard Japanese and 食べ, 行か, せ, and こ in Kansai-ben.
The short past tense form. For example: 食べた, 行った, した, and 来た.
For example: 食べて, 行って, して, and 来て.
For example: 行こう in standard Japanese and 行こ in Kansai-ben.
For example: 食べられる, 行ける, できる, and 来られる.
Abbreviation for i-adjective--an adjective that ends with an い. For example: 大きい, 高い, 新しい.
Abbreviation for na-adjective--and adjective that ends with a な. For example: 静かな, 便利な, きれいな.
In Japanese, essentially all of the "hiragana sounds" are one mora (with things like しゃ, きょ, and ん also counting as one). For example: いぬ has two moras and かんさいべんきょう has 8 moras.
The relative tone of a sound.
Where the pitch? of a word starts to fall.
When a voiced sound becomes voiceless. For example: the word です ("desu") is pronounced as "des" in standard Japanese.
For our purposes, when a vowel sound in a word exerts influence on the preceding vowel sound and makes it similar to itself.
Verbal and non-verbal responses by a listener, such as "へえ〜" and eye contact.
